risks.description: An approval recorded in memory may not survive a service restart, violating the promise that approval state survives a re-read of persisted state.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-002 approval state survives a re-read of persisted state

risks.description: Two simultaneous approvals of the same invoice could create duplicate or inconsistent durable records instead of a single approval.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 approving an invoice records the approval durably

risks.description: Approving an invoice id that does not exist could durably record a spurious approval for a non-existent invoice.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 approving an invoice records the approval durably

risks.description: Re-issuing an approval after a restart could produce a second durable approval record rather than remaining a single idempotent approval.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-002 approval state survives a re-read of persisted state

risks.description: A malformed approval request body could corrupt or partially write persisted approval state.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 approving an invoice records the approval durably

scenarios.title: Approval survives an api service restart and re-read of persisted state
scenarios.purpose: Verify that an approval recorded through the endpoint is still present in persisted state after the api service is fully restarted, which is the direct promise of AC-APPROVAL-002.
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses a scenario-unique invoice id (W2R1) that no other scenario touches; no shared row is mutated so it cannot contaminate concurrent scenarios. No approved command can delete state, so isolation is by unique id rather than teardown.
scenarios.rationale: Every prior approve request timed out; even once responsive, durability across a restart is the load-bearing behavior in AC-APPROVAL-002 and is not covered by the in-session persistence scenario.
expected_observations: POST /approve returns 200 and the invoice is recorded approved before restart
After the api service restart, re-reading persisted state still shows W2R1 as approved
forbidden_observations: W2R1 shows pending or missing after restart
Persisted state loses the approval record after restart

scenarios.title: Two simultaneous approvals of the same invoice record a single durable approval
scenarios.purpose: Exercise a race: issue two approve requests for the same invoice at the same instant and confirm persisted state holds exactly one approval, not a duplicated or inconsistent record.
scenarios.isolation_note: Contends only on scenario-unique invoice id W2R2; must not run concurrently with other scenarios touching the same id, which none do.
scenarios.rationale: Idempotency was only checked as sequential double-approve; a genuine simultaneous race can still double-write durable state and is untested.
expected_observations: Both concurrent requests complete without error
Persisted state shows W2R2 approved exactly once with no duplicate or conflicting record
forbidden_observations: State shows two separate approval records for W2R2
State shows an error/duplicate marker for W2R2

scenarios.title: Approving a non-existent invoice does not record a spurious approval
scenarios.purpose: Confirm that POSTing an approval for an invoice id that was never created does not durably persist an approved record for it.
scenarios.isolation_note: References a never-created id W2R3-NOPE; a correct implementation writes nothing, so there is nothing to clean up.
scenarios.rationale: AC-APPROVAL-001 scopes durability to approving an invoice; approving something that is not an invoice should not fabricate durable state.
expected_observations: The endpoint rejects approval of an unknown invoice (non-2xx)
No approved record exists for W2R3-NOPE in persisted state
forbidden_observations: Persisted state contains an approved record for the unknown invoice
The endpoint returns 200 for a non-existent invoice

scenarios.title: Re-approving after a restart keeps a single durable approval
scenarios.purpose: After an approval survives a restart, re-issue the same approval and confirm persisted state still reflects a single approval rather than a second record.
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses scenario-unique invoice id W2R4; no other scenario references it.
scenarios.rationale: Combines re-read-after-restart with a repeated request to ensure idempotency holds across the persistence boundary, not just within one process lifetime.
expected_observations: Re-approving after restart leaves exactly one durable approval for W2R4
forbidden_observations: A second/duplicate approval record appears for W2R4 after re-approval
State reverts to pending after the second approval

scenarios.title: Malformed approval request body does not corrupt persisted state
scenarios.purpose: Send an approval with a malformed JSON body and confirm the endpoint rejects it without writing a partial or corrupt approval record.
scenarios.isolation_note: Targets scenario-unique invoice id W2R5; a correct implementation writes nothing on rejection, so no teardown is needed.
scenarios.rationale: AC-APPROVAL-001 requires durable recording of valid approvals; a malformed body must not be able to leave the store in a half-written approved state.
expected_observations: The endpoint rejects the malformed body with a 4xx
No approved record is persisted for W2R5
forbidden_observations: Persisted state shows W2R5 approved after a malformed request
A partial/corrupt record for W2R5 appears in state

unresolved_questions: All prior approve requests in this run timed out (endpoint never returned), so it is unclear whether the approval endpoint is reachable at all; if it remains unresponsive, none of these scenarios can reach their state assertions. This looks like a builder/service availability issue rather than a missing scenario.

The acceptance criteria do not state the expected response for approving a non-existent invoice (404 vs 400 vs 200-with-no-effect); gen-approve-unknown-invoice assumes rejection. If the product intends a different contract, this requirement should be made explicit rather than inferred.

No approved command can delete or reset persisted approval state, so mutating scenarios rely on unique invoice ids for isolation; if the state store is not keyed per-invoice this assumption may not hold.
